The investigation leads us to Brazil. A drought was happening there. People had also stopped hoping that the next harvest would be better. “Will there be enough beans?” Before we think about how to brew them, we must ask if there will be any beans to brew at all.

We turn the pages of the record and find this. In February, before summer, New York’s Arabica coffee futures price reached a record high. This was not the price of ground coffee in stores. It was the market price for trading coffee beans. The market alarm had already sounded.

“So, were tariffs not to blame?” No. That would be deciding too soon, too. Reuters also reported that U.S. tariffs put in place during summer raised the price of the beans themselves. They did play a part. But we must put events in the right order.

union_ok_not_verified.canonical:
“If the boss wants it, things move fast.” It is a familiar hope in meetings and business talks. But talks about joining Tesla and SpaceX may bring the opposite result. You think you have pressed the gas, but the brake lights come on. People are starting to worry about this kind of change.

Musk supported joining the two companies. He called it “a good idea.” But he says the choice should be left to special committees at both companies. Do not decide too soon. There are still steps between “he supports it” and “the merger is decided.”

According to Reuters, a person who knows about the talks is worried. They worry that Musk’s support and the public announcement of the talks may make shareholders look more closely. This could slow the talks. Support from a big name does not always make things move ahead quickly. This is not a report that the talks have already slowed.

Shareholders must also follow certain steps to approve it. For some mergers and other matters, SpaceX’s articles of incorporation set rules. Holders of “Class B” shares must vote as a separate group and approve it. Other required approvals are needed too. Musk’s support is not a pass that opens every gate.

We do not know if talks will really be delayed this time. So watch not only, “Does Musk support it?” but also, “How will others react?” Will cheers help things move forward, or will closer checks make people drive carefully? A big name’s words can fire the starting gun or give people a reason to stop. Since someone has spoken in favor, we must watch others’ next moves in these talks.

union_ok_not_verified.canonical: First thing every morning, I see the kids who come to the nurse's office. “I'm sleepy,” they say. “My head hurts,” they say. The other day, a student was resting on the bed. Their phone screen glowed beside the pillow. When I hear they stayed up until morning, I don't know what to say. I also think about one student. After their phone was taken away at school, they stopped coming to see me. If they don't come, does that mean they are okay? A teacher asked me, “If we ban phones, will fewer kids come to the nurse's office?” I could not answer. If the school bans phones during breaks too, will it think the problem is solved? That scares me. I don't take phones away in the nurse's office. I want to keep a place where kids can talk about what happened at night. After the phones are off-limits, who will listen to that child?
